title: Cross-asset information flow, contagion and nonlinear dependence: literature for an amendment to the 1962-2002 read
status: literature memo; no project data read or computed; power figures are design arithmetic
cut_short: Elicit unavailable (api_access_denied); searched via web instead

claims.claim: For jointly Gaussian processes Granger causality F equals twice transfer entropy; no extra for nonlinear extensions under Gaussianity; no general TE significance distribution known
claims.source: Barnett, Barrett, Seth 2009, arXiv 0910.4514, eq. 13, pp. 6-8

claims.claim: Plug-in TE null bias approx C^l (C^k-1)(C-1)/(2N); strong positive bias at T=100, visible at T=1000
claims.source: Kirkley, arXiv 2506.16215 v3, eq. S34, Figs. 2-3

claims.claim: Transfer entropy defined as KL deviation from the generalized Markov property; finite sample deflects estimates
Kernel Granger: linear Granger in feature space via Gram matrix projection; Bonferroni-filtered eigenvectors; critical coupling scales N^-0.5
claims.source: Marinazzo, Pellicoro, Stramaglia 2008, arXiv 0711.2643, eqs. 2-5, Fig. 2

claims.claim: PCMCI controls false positives under autocorrelation; i.i.d. permutation and pre-whitening fail in multivariate case; climate example T=468 months partial corr ~0.10 p~0.036; finite-sample power for nonlinear tests mostly impossible to derive
Neural Granger evaluated by AUROC over penalty sweep, no p-value; VAR(1) coef 0.1 AUROC 91.6 at T=250
claims.source: Tank et al., arXiv 1802.05842 v2, Tables 1-2

claims.claim: Hiemstra-Jones test over-rejects, reject rate tends to 1 as sample grows (citing Diks-Panchenko 2005)
Diks-Panchenko 2006 replace the HJ global statistic with local measures and shrinking bandwidth; size near nominal

Oil price change predicts US monthly equity return: slope -0.086, t -3.57, 1973-10..2003-04, 355 months; world -0.081 t -2.90; with world returns as regressor only 5 developed markets significant, US not among them
claims.source: Driesprong, Jacobsen, Maat, ERIM WP ERS-2003-082, pp. 8-9, Table I

claims.claim: Industries lead the market by up to two months (metal coefficient -0.106; 2-sd shock = 1.39% = 32% of market vol), 1972-2001

Correlation bias under heteroskedasticity: rho = rho* sqrt(1+delta)/sqrt(1+delta rho*^2); adjustment requires no endogeneity and no omitted aggregate shock; contagion incidence falls dramatically after adjustment
claims.source: Forbes, Rigobon NBER WP 7267, pp. 1-2, 11-12, fn 7 (OCR text layer)

claims.claim: H.10 rates are noon buying rates in New York
Past bond returns predict equity positively, equity predicts bonds negatively, 20 countries 1980-2016; cross-asset TSMOM Sharpe 45% higher
Lagged US returns predict non-US returns, not the reverse, 1980:02-2010:12
Commodity-currency exchange rates forecast commodity prices out of sample; reverse less robust
Industrial metal returns predict stock returns, sign depends on business cycle
Over a third of post-2008 predictors fail in-sample; half of the rest poor out-of-sample
No popular predictor beats the historical mean out of sample
Sign restrictions give small but economically meaningful OOS R2
Anomaly returns 26% lower out of sample, 58% lower post publication
Overlapping long-horizon estimators almost perfectly correlated under null with persistent regressors
i.i.d. bootstrap for HSIC fails for random processes; wild bootstrap consistent for time series
CCM convergence limited by noise and data length; fails under synchronisation
claims.source: Sugihara et al. 2012 supplement; Monster et al. 2016

claims.claim: Absorption-ratio spikes preceded most significant US drawdowns
Ridgeless random-feature market timing gain is mechanical volatility-timed momentum
claims.source: Nagel 2025 BFI WP 2025-104 on Kelly-Malamud-Zhou JF 2024

claims.claim: Generalized-FEVD spillovers across US stock, bond, FX, commodity volatility 1999-2010 limited until 2007
Frequency-domain connectedness (short/medium/long cycles)
Tail spillovers stronger than at the median
Correlation rises in bear markets, not with volatility per se
Most published cross-asset predictability evidence read here is estimated inside 1962-2002

family.name: bonds -> equity
family.statistic: OLS t of x1 in r_e(t+1) ~ 1 + Z_t + x1_t; x1 = 12-month excess return of US 10y proxy; one-sided +
family.null: beta=0; restricted-model residual bootstrap, paired stationary blocks mean 12, 10000 draws, seed 20261125
family.why: linear: sign prior, slow-rebalancing mechanism; lookback is our registered choice

family.name: energy -> equity
family.statistic: as H1 with x2 = last-month excess return of equal-weight energy futures composite; one-sided -
family.why: linear as in Driesprong et al.; labelled replication (in-window overlap)

family.name: commodity currencies -> commodities (second book)
family.statistic: OLS t of x3 in rc(t+1) ~ 1 + rc_t + x3_t; x3 = equal-weight AUD, CAD excess return; one-sided +

family.name: Gram-matrix absorption-ratio spike -> equity
family.statistic: coefficient of Spike_t (AR 15d - AR 252d >= 1 sd of 252d) of 5 composites in H1-form regression; one-sided -
family.null: as H1, AR rebuilt per draw from block-resampled daily composites
family.why: nonlinear (threshold on second-moment state); out-of-window prior on equity sectors, extrapolated

family.name: nonlinear information beyond linear (kernel)
family.statistic: HSIC(linear residual, X_t), Gaussian kernels, median-heuristic bandwidth fixed at registration
family.null: independence; wild bootstrap for time series
family.power: unknown; simulate before read on synthetic data; expected low
family.why: omnibus nonlinear check; monthly T too small for TE/MI

family.name: tail (quantile) Granger
family.statistic: rank-score/Wald test that bond, energy, FX slopes jointly 0 in tau=0.10 quantile regression of r_e(t+1) on Z_t and one-month returns
family.null: as H1 with restricted quantile model
family.power: simulate before read; below mean-regression power

family_rules.controls: Z_t = equity month-t return, core state at end of month t
family_rules.multiplicity: Holm at family 0.10; programme 0.10/N reported; N += 6
family_rules.oos: recursive OOS R2 from 1980-01 with Campbell-Thompson restrictions, reported
family_rules.owner_ruling_needed: H1, H2, H4, H6 are exposure-timing research on a spent target (US equity 1962-2002); CLAUDE.md rule 17
